eva: Heads-up — after yesterday's microbatch tuning rollout we see improved median latency for completions but a noticeable p99/p999 spike for streaming chat. Can we triage?

sam: saw that in dashboards, p99 up ~40-60ms on some models, p999 occasionally +200ms. linking traces now.

cheng: interesting — did the rollout change kernel selection thresholds or just mb_size defaults?

eva: we reduced default mb_size from 12->6 for streaming pools and enabled more aggressive continuous-batching. Kernels unchanged.

lucy: quick summary from perf-bot run: streaming requests now hit small microbatches more often which increases kernel-switch overhead and reduces KV cache reuse.

perf-bot: ``
PROFILE SUMMARY (sample window 5m)
- overall qps: 980 -> 1020 (+4%)
- p50 lat: 28ms -> 24ms (-4ms)
- p95 lat: 74ms -> 68ms (-6ms)
- p99 lat: 132ms -> 188ms (+56ms)
- p999 lat: 240ms -> 430ms (+190ms)

KERNEL TIMINGS (streaming paths):
- attention_kernel_switch: 0.9ms -> 2.4ms avg (calls up)
- kv_cache_lookup: 0.4ms -> 0.9ms avg (misses up)
- tail_flush_penalty: 0.8ms -> 3.6ms (more frequent)
``

sam: that matches what i see in trace slices — many streaming sessions trigger a kernel fallback (FP16->INT8 path) mid-request which stalls tail tokens.

cheng: why fallback mid-request? should be stable per-request unless sequence length or kv profile changes.

eva: hypothesis: microbatch coalescing sometimes merges streaming tokens with short non-streaming completions on same worker; kernel selection is per-batch and can switch if incoming batch composition changes (we merged some fallback logic in last week).

lucy: also KV cache TTL heuristics got loosened in the tuning: small mb -> more interleaving -> less contiguous KV hits. Miss ratio for long chat sessions jumped from 3% -> 9%.

sam: can we repro locally with small harness? what config?

eva: repro config I used:
```
model: gpt-open-13b
pool: streaming-small
microbatch_size: 6
continuous_batching: enabled
kv_cache_ttl_ms: 50
kernel_policy: dynamic
```
run with 500 concurrent streams, message lengths 8-64 tokens.

perf-bot: attached trace ids: tracex/7721, tracex/7727 for p99 examples.

cheng: quick fix options:
- widen mb_size for streaming back to 10 (favors kv locality but ups median)
- make kernel selection stable per-request (sticky) to avoid mid-request switches
- tighten kv_cache_ttl for streaming so entries live longer per session

lucy: sticky kernel selection seems low-risk. It prevents mid-request stalls at cost of slightly suboptimal kernel for mixed batches.

sam: can we quantify tradeoff? if we glue kernel per-request, what happens to throughput?

eva: ran a microbenchmark: sticky kernel per-request -> p99 for streaming drops ~90ms; p50 increases ~2ms; overall throughput -1.5%.

cheng: good tradeoff. another idea: hybrid batching heuristic: for streaming mark requests as "streaming-hot" and prefer same-worker colocations (improve KV hits) + allow larger mb_size if the batch is homogeneous.

lucy: config proposal patch:
```
# runtime config snippet
batching:
  policies:
    - name: streaming_hot
      predicate: request.is_streaming == true
      microbatch_target: 10
      stick_kernel_per_request: true
      prefer_kv_colocation: true
```

eva: I'll prototype that. also adding a lightweight counter to avoid over-bloating worker latency: only apply prefer_kv_colocation if worker.queue_depth < 200.

sam: regression checklist for rollout:
1) A/B with 10% traffic -> monitor p50/p95/p99/p999 per-model
2) check kernel_switch_rate metric and kv_miss_rate
3) rollback trigger: p99 increase > 30% sustained for 3 minutes

cheng: +1. Also add trace sampling for sessions with p99 to ensure we capture kernel-switch patterns.

lucy: FYI I found one trace where a client streamed 1 token every 200ms; that pattern kills ms-level batching and increases tail. Suggest client-side coalescing guidance too.

eva: good call — adding a note to docs: "for streaming chat, prefer micro-batchable client sends (batch small groups) or use 100ms coalescing window".

perf-bot: deploy scheduled: canary will run at 10:45 UTC. ops-bot: `deploy: staging/streaming-hot-fix`

sam: thanks — i'll watch p99 dashboards. eva/ cheng, ping me if you need extra traces.

eva: will do. thanks team :rocket:
